about.bio:
I am an Information Systems Engineer graduated from UTN (GPA 8.55/10, Flag Escort of Honor 2025) and a Full Stack & Mobile Engineer experienced in building end-to-end software: from database architecture to the final user experience.

Throughout my career, I led the digital transformation platform for the Science & Technology Department at UTN-FRRe, developed internationally awarded Web3 solutions like Dosel (1st Place Stellar Track at NEA TECH 2026), launched mobile apps published on Google Play (DateBox, Chess Study, Elepad), and built high-traffic commercial platforms like Mandadito and DÚO Propiedades.

I believe great software exists to solve tangible problems for people and businesses, never to add unnecessary complexity. Currently, I am looking to join engineering teams and product companies where I can contribute technical ownership across the stack, solid architectural judgment, and a commitment to shipping resilient, scalable value to production.

projects.arch_desc: The platform is structured under a decoupled and multi-layered software architecture design, separating presentation logic (React Frontend), business logic and persistence (Node.js/Express Backend with Prisma ORM), and the relational database engine (PostgreSQL). Everything is deployed independently in the cloud.
projects.db_schema_desc: The data modeling was designed following relational normalization principles to ensure referential integrity and optimize complex queries for nested relationships among researchers, projects, agreements, and disbursements.
projects.db_der_desc: Initial conceptual model designed in Draw.io and formally validated with the Secretariat directors to structure data flows and cardinalities.
projects.db_physical_desc: Physical database schema deployed in production using PostgreSQL and Prisma ORM, structured with primary keys, foreign keys, unique constraints, and optimized indexes.
projects.devops_arch_desc: The system is designed under a decoupled, containerized microservices architecture. It utilizes Azure Container Instances (ACI) as an independent, elastic host for each component: an interactive Next.js frontend, a high-performance Flask REST API, and a distributed Redis Alpine cache engine, all securely communicating under an internal subnet with persistent cloud storage.
projects.devops_pipeline_desc: The automated workflow is triggered in parallel on every push to the production branch. It runs automated backend tests with Pytest (utilizing a temporary local Redis service) and, upon success, builds optimized multi-stage Docker images and deploys them to Azure Container Instances (ACI) using Azure CLI commands.
projects.devops_parallel_desc: Shows how a single push to the 'docker' branch triggers the execution of both the unit tests and the deployment pipelines in parallel and independently.
projects.devops_success_desc: Summary panel of a successful deployment pipeline run, displaying the triggering commit, the corresponding branch, the success status, and the total execution duration.
projects.devops_detail_desc: Orchestrated sequence of steps inside the CD pipeline: initialization, secure login to Azure ACR, accelerated compilation via Docker Buildx, image push, and dynamic container recreation.
projects.devops_app_desc: Functional views of the deployed web application: the blind voting screen for AI-generated descriptions and the dynamic dashboard with bar charts (using Recharts) displaying model performance statistics stored persistently.
projects.devops_voting_desc: Interactive module where users vote blindly and anonymously on the description that best fits the product.
projects.devops_stats_desc: Dynamic chart displaying the performance and cumulative votes of each AI model in the database.
projects.k8s_cluster_desc: Overview of the system's three layers: Application Layer (Next.js Frontend, Flask Backend x2, Redis), Observability Stack (Grafana, Prometheus, Tempo, OTEL Collector), and K8s infrastructure (Traefik, CoreDNS, kube-state-metrics). Each component exposes its endpoints and communicates internally via ClusterIP, with external access via NodePort.
projects.k8s_ha_desc: 2 Flask backend replicas with mandatory podAntiAffinity — never on the same worker. Readiness probes every 5s and liveness probes every 10s guarantee auto-restart on failure. The NodePort service load balances traffic round-robin between both replicas.
projects.k8s_observability_desc: We implemented a complete observability stack with three pillars: Metrics (Prometheus + kube-state-metrics + cAdvisor → Grafana), Distributed Traces (Backend instrumented with OpenTelemetry SDK → OTEL Collector → Tempo → Grafana with TraceQL), and real-time dashboards with a 30-second refresh window.
projects.k8s_flow_desc: Full sequence diagram showing the lifecycle of a request: User → Frontend → NodePort → Backend (with load balancing) → Redis (cache) → OTEL Collector → Tempo for traces, while Prometheus scrapes /metrics every 5s for Grafana dashboards.
projects.k8s_metrics_desc: Prometheus scrapes prometheus_flask_exporter on :10000/metrics, kube-state-metrics on :8080, and cAdvisor (built into K3s). Key metrics: RPS (all/business), p95/p50 latency, CPU usage, memory, and pod restarts.
projects.k8s_tracing_desc: The backend sends traces via OTLP gRPC to the OTEL Collector, which exports them to Tempo. Grafana queries them using TraceQL, capturing Trace ID, Span ID, duration, status, and HTTP attributes.
projects.bi_modeling_desc: The multidimensional model was designed following the 'multidim' conceptual methodology and the relational physical schema in SQL Server. We defined daily granularity for thorough tracking of retail sales transactions and record production costs.
projects.bi_conceptual_desc: Global logical structure unifying the two main fact tables (HechoVentas and HechoProducciones) with the key dimensions to answer strategic ROI and market coverage queries.
projects.bi_physical_desc: Relational database diagram implemented in SQL Server, showing auto-incrementing surrogate keys, foreign keys with strict referential integrity constraints, and default surrogate records (-1) for nulls.
projects.bi_etl_title: Part 2: Integration & ETL Pipelines in Integration Services (SSIS)
projects.bi_etl_desc: We developed ETL packages in SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS) organized hierarchically to guarantee efficient, idempotent initial bulk loads and periodic incremental loads.
projects.bi_control_flow_desc: Main control flow orchestrated in SSIS for the bulk load: truncating the DW, inserting surrogate default rows, procedural generation of DimTiempo, and sequential loading of leaf, intermediate, and fact tables.
projects.bi_scd_desc: Implementation of the Slowly Changing Dimensions component in SSIS. SCD Type 1 was defined to overwrite basic modified attributes, and SCD Type 2 was applied in DimArtista and DimBanda to track historical changes with effective dates (from/to).
projects.bi_olap_title: Part 3: Multidimensional Cubes (SSAS) & Power BI Dashboards
projects.bi_olap_desc: We harnessed the Data Warehouse by building an OLAP multidimensional database in Analysis Services (SSAS) and connecting it to interactive executive dashboards in Power BI.
projects.bi_cube_desc: OLAP multidimensional cube design with integrated complex hierarchies (geographical store views and temporal views), measure groups, and custom MDX calculations to track Unmet Demand.
projects.bi_powerbi_desc: Executive dashboard consolidated in Power BI that interactively presents ROI analysis, sales by genre, geographical maps, and compliance metrics, enabling Drill-down, Roll-up, Slice, and Dice operations.

dosel.clientOrContext: 1st Place Stellar Track · NEA TECH Ideathon 2026
dosel.title: DOSEL
dosel.subtitle: Satellite Verification & Blockchain Traceability for Carbon Credits
dosel.description: Web3 platform tackling greenwashing: Sentinel-2 satellite oracle and Rust smart contracts on Stellar (Soroban) that freeze issuance upon deforestation and enable atomic buy-and-retire.
dosel.long_description:
Dosel is a Web3 and satellite remote sensing platform designed to bring radical transparency and traceability to the voluntary carbon credit market across native forests in the Gran Chaco and NEA region.

Instead of relying on self-declarations or bureaucratic on-site audits that take months and fail to ensure continuity, Dosel implements an automated biophysical oracle in Python: it processes multispectral imagery from Sentinel-2 satellites (at 10-meter resolution) over the GPS boundaries of registered parcels (such as El Impenetrable or Taco Pozo) and calculates cloud-free vegetation index (NDVI).

Only if the forest remains conserved and thriving, smart contracts written in Rust on Stellar (Soroban SDK) issue representative carbon tokens (GreenTon, 1 GTON = 1 tCO2e). If the oracle detects a critical NDVI drop, the contract automatically freezes the parcel and stops further issuance. The platform features a decentralized marketplace with smart custody and atomic retirement (Buy & Retire), bypassing intermediaries, preventing double counting, and generating verifiable on-chain certificates.
dosel.challenge: In the traditional voluntary carbon market, the lack of continuous verification fuels distrust and greenwashing: on-site audits are slow and costly, making it nearly impossible to ensure that a parcel backing carbon credits hasn't been cleared months after issuance.
dosel.solution: We built Dosel during the 3-day NEA TECH 2026 Ideathon (winning 1st Place in the Stellar Track): a Python oracle processes Sentinel-2 imagery to gauge canopy vitality and record verified batches in Soroban. Rust smart contracts handle escrow and let corporations purchase and retire credits in a single atomic, irreversible transaction using Freighter Wallet.

highlights.label: Stellar Track · NEA TECH Ideathon ($500 USD award by SDF & BAF)
Satellite monitoring at 10m resolution (NDVI)
On-chain freeze upon detected vegetation loss
Irreversible atomic purchase & retirement without resale

key_features.title: Rust Smart Contracts (Soroban)

key_features.title: Atomic Buy & Retire
key_features.description: Marketplace function executing payment (XLM SAC) and irreversible retirement/burning of credits on behalf of the buyer in a single atomic transaction.

key_features.description: React, Vite, and TypeScript SPA integrated with Stellar SDK and Freighter Wallet, featuring a real-time radar for local environmental news and satellite passes.

features: GreenTon smart contract in Rust with soroban-sdk 29: minting strictly conditioned on satellite oracle signatures per parcel and period.
On-chain contingency logic: automatic parcel freezing if NDVI drops below 0.400 or experiences a decline greater than 0.150 against baseline.
Marketplace smart contract: decentralized custody of listed batches and atomic buy_and_retire function with instant token retirement.
Geospatial processing pipeline in Python using pystac-client, Microsoft Planetary Computer, rasterio, and numpy across Sentinel-2 B04 and B08 bands.
Responsive Web3 frontend with React 19, TypeScript, and Vite, connecting to Soroban RPC and Freighter Wallet.
Gran Chaco Radar module integrating land cover datasets (Impact Observatory) and RSS environmental news aggregation.
Complete on-chain traceability in Stellar Expert: over 61,000 GTON tokens minted and verified atomic burn purchases on Testnet.
dosel.arch_title: Decentralized Architecture: Satellite Oracle & Stellar Soroban
dosel.arch_desc: Dosel decouples biophysical data collection from on-chain governance across three layers: (1) Satellite Layer: Sentinel-2 and Planetary Computer STAC catalog provide optical reflectance data processed in Python with Rasterio. (2) Blockchain Layer: Rust smart contracts (Soroban SDK) enforce business logic, parcel escrow, and automated freezing on Stellar Testnet, ensuring immutability and negligible gas fees. (3) Application Layer: The React/TypeScript web app queries network state via Soroban RPC and enables buyers to connect Freighter Wallet to transact directly without intermediaries.

duo-propiedades.title: DÚO Propiedades
duo-propiedades.subtitle: Real Estate Platform, Interactive Catalog & Management Dashboard
duo-propiedades.description: Web platform designed to digitize the property catalog, receive online valuation requests, and manage listings effortlessly from any device.
duo-propiedades.long_description:
DÚO Propiedades is a comprehensive digital solution designed to digitize the property catalog, attract new owners via online valuation requests, and optimize the commercial operations of the agency in Pirané, Formosa.

The system was architected using a decoupled and scalable Serverless infrastructure, hosting database, authentication, media storage, and server environments on high-availability cloud platforms.

Phase 1 is fully completed and deployed to production, delivering an institutional mobile-first landing page, a properties catalog with advanced search and filtering, a web form to capture valuation requests, and a secured internal administrative panel to manage property inventory (CRUD) and dynamic states (Available, Reserved, Under Negotiation).
duo-propiedades.challenge: The real estate agency needed a clear digital channel to receive inquiries from ad campaigns, showcase an up-to-date catalog of houses, land, and commercial spaces, and capture property owners interested in appraisals or selling while keeping operational costs low.
duo-propiedades.solution: We built a mobile-first platform with three integrated modules: a commercial home page with quick actions (Buy, Rent, Appraise), a public catalog with dynamic filters and live statuses, and an internal panel where the agency uploads photos, edits listings, and manages valuation requests.

highlights.label: Buying, Renting, and Online Valuation
Statuses: Available, Reserved, or Negotiating
Internal panel to upload and edit properties
Tailored for mobile and social media inquiries

key_features.title: Property Listings with Live Status
key_features.description: Each property displays a photo gallery, available utilities, technical specifications, map location, and real-time commercial status badges.

key_features.title: Online Valuation Request Flow
key_features.description: Guided form for property owners looking to appraise or sell their property, capturing key characteristics and their WhatsApp contact.

key_features.title: Internal Administration Dashboard

features: Responsive, mobile-first web interface built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript for SEO optimization and advertising campaigns.
Interactive catalog with smart dynamic search and advanced filtering by property type (Houses, Land, Commercial), location, price, and size (m²).
Secure internal administration dashboard protected by Supabase Auth.
Complete CRUD module for easy property listing uploads and editing (technical details, amenities, and photos).
Instant real-time status controller (Available, Reserved, Under Negotiation) immediately reflected on the public site.
Valuation flow to capture owner contact details and WhatsApp numbers, with centralized tracking for the administrator.
100% serverless architecture utilizing Supabase Storage for property media and Vercel for scalable hosting.
duo-propiedades.arch_desc: The system was designed with a decoupled serverless topology that guarantees high availability and elastic scalability. The landing page and CRUD panel run on Next.js hosted on Vercel, while data, authentication, and media are served from Supabase (PostgreSQL and Storage), enabling a modern cloud infrastructure without unnecessary fixed operational overhead.

datebox.clientOrContext: Own Product · Pre-incubated at EBT Chaco Program
datebox.title: DateBox
datebox.subtitle: Mobile App for Group Outings & Local Merchant Platform
datebox.description: Mobile app and merchant portal that simplifies planning outings with friends: matches free time slots, suggests local plans with AI, and connects venues with groups.
datebox.long_description:
Datebox is a mobile platform designed to simplify the organization of group outings and social events. The application automates finding open slots in friends' calendars and utilizes smart recommendation algorithms to suggest restaurants, events, and local spots.

Besides facilitating group coordination and reducing indecisiveness, it integrates a B2B advertising model that enables local businesses and venues to promote their services directly to groups with high consumption intent in real-time.

Currently, the project features a cross-platform mobile application and a web administration portal for local businesses.
datebox.challenge: Coordinating a group outing often gets stuck trying to match everyone's schedule and deciding where to go. Meanwhile, local restaurants, bars, and cultural venues struggle to reach groups actively planning an outing in their area.
datebox.solution: We built DateBox: a mobile app where group members mark their free time slots to find matches automatically, receive AI-powered activity suggestions based on preferences and budget, save shared photo albums, and discover local promotions published through a web merchant portal.

highlights.label: Cross-platform mobile app + Merchant web portal
Automatic detection of shared free time slots
Suggestions tailored to taste, area, and budget
Web dashboard for bars, restaurants, and events

chess-study.clientOrContext: Mobile App on Google Play Store & Open Source Web
chess-study.title: Chess Study
chess-study.subtitle: Chess Book PDF Reader, Analysis Board & On-Device AI Scanner
chess-study.description: Web and mobile application (published on Google Play Store) combining a 60 FPS split-screen chess PDF reader with an interactive board and an on-device computer vision scanner (ONNX / CNN) that detects positions with a single click.
chess-study.long_description:
Chess Study is a mobile and web app designed specifically to eliminate friction when studying chess with digital books: it unifies a high-performance 60 FPS PDF reader and an interactive analysis board with optical diagram recognition (Chess OCR) powered by 100% local AI on a single split-screen.

Instead of constantly switching between heavy PDF readers and external analysis software while manually setting up positions piece by piece, Chess Study allows users to click any diagram printed in the book (or paste a screenshot from clipboard via Ctrl+V) so a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) running directly in the browser via ONNX Runtime Web and WebAssembly classifies the 64 squares and reconstructs the FEN position in milliseconds—without transmitting data to external servers.

The application is packaged as an installable PWA with Service Workers and published on Google Play Store via Trusted Web Activity (TWA / signed Android App Bundle with Digital Asset Links). It also features complete offline persistence through IndexedDB: open your own books or the built-in classical library (like Roberto Grau's Treatise) and always resume from the exact page you left off.
chess-study.challenge: Studying chess with digital books often requires switching back and forth between a PDF viewer and an analysis board in another window, losing reading focus and wasting time setting up positions by hand.
chess-study.solution: We built a 60 FPS split-screen application published on Google Play Store: read PDF books smoothly on one side with automatic local storage, and analyze variations on an interactive board with FAN algebraic notation on the other. Clicking any diagram in the PDF triggers a lightweight computer vision model that recognizes the pieces and sets up the board immediately.

highlights.label: Published on Google Play Store (signed TWA / AAB)
On-device Chess OCR scanning (ONNX WebAssembly)
Smooth large PDF rendering via Web Workers
IndexedDB local persistence without servers

key_features.description: Convolutional Neural Network (1.3 MB CNN) executed with ONNX Runtime Web on WebAssembly that classifies squares and reconstructs FEN on the fly without cloud requests.

key_features.title: Adjustable Split-Screen Layout

key_features.title: Google Play Distribution & Offline Storage
key_features.description: Published on Google Play Store via TWA with Digital Asset Links, PDF.js v4.2 reader in a dedicated Web Worker, and IndexedDB book caching.

features: Published on Google Play Store as a Trusted Web Activity (TWA) with Service Workers and offline web manifest.
Client-side computer vision: lightweight CNN model (1.3 MB) running in WebAssembly with ONNX Runtime Web to classify all 64 squares and output FEN.
Contrast gradient edge detection algorithm to capture diagrams with one click or direct clipboard pasting (Ctrl+V).
Full chess logic with FAN notation (SVG figurines), move history navigation, and legal move validation via chess.js.
Precompiled PDF.js v4.2 isolated inside a Web Worker to handle 300+ page books without UI stuttering.
IndexedDB persistence for custom book uploads, Grau's classical Treatise library, and reading position memory.
Visual customizer: multiple board themes (Cyberpunk, Ocean, Emerald, Wood) with Dark/Light mode integration.
chess-study.arch_title: Architecture: Offline Computer Vision, Web Workers & Mobile Distribution
chess-study.arch_desc: The application pairs React 19, Vite, and Tailwind CSS with a privacy-first, offline-ready architecture. Instead of processing images on latency-prone cloud servers, AI inference runs 100% on the client through ONNX Runtime Web compiled to WebAssembly. Heavy PDF document rendering is offloaded to a dedicated Web Worker, maintaining a solid 60 FPS refresh rate. For mobile distribution, a TWA wrapper packages the PWA into a signed Android App Bundle, enabling direct Google Play Store installation with immersive fullscreen support.

elepad.clientOrContext: Engineering Capstone Project · Google Play Store
elepad.title: Elepad
elepad.subtitle: Mobile App for Older Adults, Cognitive Games & AI Family Memory Album
elepad.description: Mobile app published on Google Play that connects older adults with their families through an accessible interface, daily memory games, and an AI-assisted family album.
elepad.long_description:
Elepad is a mobile application designed to foster the emotional, cognitive, and social well-being of senior citizens through an accessible and interactive digital environment. Through a simplified interface and innovative tools such as AI-powered memory synthesis (Google Gemini), it seeks to build meaningful intergenerational bridges within the family.

Originating as a winning proposal at the Latin American Innovation Rally 2024 (3rd place, Social Impact), it evolved into the Final Degree Project for the Information Systems Engineering program (UTN-FRRe). Available on the Google Play Store.
elepad.challenge: Most modern mobile apps use complex menus and small text that make them frustrating for older adults to navigate, creating a barrier to digital inclusion and everyday connection with their families.
elepad.solution: Born at the 2024 Latin American Innovation Rally (3rd place in Social Impact) and developed as our Information Systems Engineering Capstone Project, Elepad provides an accessible interface, daily cognitive stimulation games, activity tracking, and a Google Gemini module that helps turn family photos and stories into organized memories.

highlights.label: Published on the official Android store
Social Impact category at LatAm Rally 2024
Memory storytelling assisted by Google Gemini
Systems Engineering Thesis (UTN-FRRe)

key_features.title: Accessible, Senior-Friendly Interface
key_features.description: Clear typography, generous touch targets, and straightforward navigation designed so older adults can use the app comfortably.

key_features.title: Cognitive Games & Family Progress
key_features.description: Includes daily games to exercise memory, attention, and logic (Memory, Sudoku, Lights Out) with progress shared across the family group.

key_features.title: The Album: AI-Assisted Family Memories
key_features.description: Uses Google Gemini to transform everyday photos and anecdotes into warm, organized stories inside a shared family album.

key_features.title: Real-Time Family Synchronization
key_features.description: Connects family members and older adults through push notifications, Google sign-in, and secure cloud storage.

features: Cross-platform mobile development (iOS/Android/Web) using React Native, Expo, and TypeScript
Hyper-scalable Serverless Backend architecture using Cloudflare Workers, Hono, and OpenAPI validation
Comprehensive data management with Supabase: PostgreSQL database, Authentication (Google OAuth), Storage, and Realtime
AI-assisted memory synthesis and narrative album module (Google Gemini)
Monorepo structure managed with Turborepo, optimizing build and development times
Automated CI/CD pipelines via GitHub Actions targeting Cloudflare and Expo EAS
Agile development: Team management under the Scrum methodology with 7 documented releases
elepad.arch_desc: Elepad is designed under a decoupled and serverless Client/Server model, optimized to ensure high availability and hyper-scalability with minimal overhead. The cross-platform mobile application (built with React Native and Expo for Android/iOS/Web) communicates asynchronously with a stateless serverless backend implemented with Hono and OpenAPI validation, deployed on Cloudflare Workers. All data persistence, multimedia resource storage, and secure Google OAuth authentication are delegated to Supabase, secured with signed JWT tokens.
elepad.db_desc: The PostgreSQL relational database engine, hosted on Supabase, was initially structured around a simplified schema to persist users, family groups, and multimedia memories. As the project evolved and iterative Scrum development progressed, the database schema was dynamically expanded to support cognitive and memory games (Sudoku, Memory, Lights Out), user activity streaks, integrated push notification tokens, device tracking, and virtual item purchases in the in-app store.

scyt-utn.clientOrContext: Secretariat of Science & Technology — UTN Resistencia Regional Faculty
scyt-utn.title: SCyT Platform — UTN FRRe
scyt-utn.subtitle: Comprehensive Management System for Research Projects, Researchers & Agreements
scyt-utn.description: Institutional web platform unifying the Faculty's scientific administration: tracking research projects, research staff, technological agreements, and budgets.
scyt-utn.long_description:
I designed and developed the entire comprehensive web platform for the Secretariat of Science and Technology (SCyT) of the National Technological University - Resistencia Regional Faculty (UTN-FRRe). The project was conceived as a strategic solution to address the dispersion of critical information regarding researchers, projects, and agreements (which were previously managed inefficiently across isolated spreadsheets). The system centralizes and unifies all scientific administration within the Faculty, enabling detailed tracking of research projects (both internal PIDs and external), management of teaching and research personnel, and administration of technological linkages, agreements, and financial disbursements.

Formally accredited as my Supervised Professional Practice (PPS), I led the complete software development lifecycle: requirements gathering (5W+2H), conceptual analysis, relational database design (ERD), interface prototyping (UX/UI), full-stack development (React, Node.js, Express, Prisma, PostgreSQL), and continuous deployment in a Cloud environment (Render).
scyt-utn.challenge: The Secretariat managed hundreds of research projects, staff records, agreements, and financial disbursements across isolated Excel spreadsheets, making it hard to cross-reference historical data, audit budgets, or quickly check a project's status.
scyt-utn.solution: Working directly with the Secretariat's directors, I designed and built an end-to-end centralized web platform where administrative staff register projects (internal PIDs and external), assign researchers with role histories, manage technological agreements, and track every financial disbursement.

highlights.label: Projects, Researchers, Agreements, and Finance
Replaced scattered spreadsheets with one database
Requirements, design, code, and Cloud deployment
Accredited as Supervised Professional Practice

key_features.title: Scientific Project Tracking (PIDs & External)
key_features.description: Register research projects, check operational status, filter by category or period, and access complete technical records in seconds.

key_features.title: Researcher Profiles & Role History
key_features.description: Manage directors, co-directors, faculty, and fellows while preserving the full history of which projects each researcher participated in.

key_features.title: Technological Linkage & Agreements Management
key_features.description: Centralizes strategic agreements signed with external companies and institutions, linking them directly to research teams.

key_features.title: Budget & Disbursement Control
key_features.description: Records budget allocations for each project and tracks executed and pending fund disbursements with full accountability.

features: Design and implementation of the Project Management Module, allowing registration, editing, advanced search, and operational status tracking of scientific projects (internal PIDs and external).
Development of the Researchers & Members Module, enabling the assignment of directors, co-directors, and collaborators with specific roles and historical participation tracking.
Implementation of the Technological Linkages & Agreements Module, facilitating the administration of strategic agreements with external companies and entities (UVT).
Development of a Financial Management & Disbursements Module, enabling the input and tracking of budgets, project funding, and associated fund disbursements.
Development of dynamic and responsive user interfaces with React.js and Chakra UI, achieving an intuitive UX/UI organized into clear tabs and logical blocks.
Multi-layer Backend architecture with Node.js and Express.js, cleanly structured into Routes, Controllers, business logic Services, and Repositories.
Design, normalization, and logical-physical modeling of a relational PostgreSQL database with Prisma ORM, optimizing queries and managing complex nested relations.
Robust authentication and authorization system based on JSON Web Tokens (JWT) with protected routing in the backend.
Essential security practices such as cryptographic password hashing using Bcrypt.
Global state management and asynchronous request optimization using TanStack Query, achieving intelligent caching and reducing server load.
Robust, real-time form validation using React Hook Form integrated with Yup validation schemas.
Version control and collaborative workflow using Git and GitHub, along with continuous deployment (CI/CD) of services and the relational database on Render Cloud.

devops-kubernetes.title: Kubernetes & Observability
devops-kubernetes.subtitle: High-Availability Microservices Orchestration with Real-Time Monitoring
devops-kubernetes.description: Deployment of a distributed web platform on a 3-node Kubernetes cluster with fault tolerance and live metrics and tracing dashboards (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, and Grafana).
devops-kubernetes.long_description:
Academic project building on the same SmartCatalog system from TP1 (orchestration-and-observability branch), elevated to Kubernetes local orchestration (K3d) and production-grade observability. We deployed a tp2-cluster with 3 nodes (1 control-plane + 2 workers) and 2 Flask backend replicas distributed via strict podAntiAffinity — ensuring they never coexist on the same worker. The observability stack integrates three fundamental pillars: metrics with Prometheus (+ kube-state-metrics + cAdvisor), distributed traces with OpenTelemetry SDK → OTEL Collector → Tempo, and unified visualization in Grafana.

Custom business metrics (RPS, p95/p50 latency), resilience validation via resource saturation, and automated health checks were implemented. The project was delivered as a live demonstration showing the cluster operating in real time.
devops-kubernetes.challenge: When a web application experiences traffic spikes or a server node fails, the service can go offline completely if it lacks distributed replicas and real-time visibility into bottlenecks.
devops-kubernetes.solution: We orchestrated the platform across a 3-node Kubernetes cluster with replicas separated on different worker nodes so if one fails, the other keeps serving users without interruption. We also wired live Grafana dashboards tracking every request, latency, and memory metric.

highlights.label: 1 Control-Plane + 2 Workers running 8 services
Distributed replicas with automatic self-healing
Live metrics (Prometheus) + Traces (OpenTelemetry)
Real-time dashboards for traffic and p95 latency

key_features.title: Fault-Tolerant Service Continuity (High Availability)
key_features.description: The backend runs duplicated across separate nodes: if one instance fails or saturates, traffic automatically routes to the healthy replica while Kubernetes spins up a replacement.

key_features.title: End-to-End Request Tracing (Distributed Traces)
key_features.description: Follow the exact path of a user action from the web interface through the API to the Redis database to pinpoint slow operations immediately.

key_features.title: Business & Infrastructure Monitoring
key_features.description: Measures real user votes per second, 95th-percentile response times, and CPU/RAM consumption per container.

key_features.title: Stress Testing & Resource Safeguards
key_features.description: Configured memory and CPU limits per service to verify how the cluster automatically recovers under extreme load.

features: K3d 3-node cluster: 1 control-plane + 2 workers running 8 distributed microservices (Frontend, Backend x2, Redis, Prometheus, Tempo, OTEL Collector, Grafana, kube-state-metrics)

Guaranteed High Availability: podAntiAffinity with requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution prevents the 2 backend replicas from sharing a node. Readiness probes every 5s + liveness probes every 10s for automatic auto-restart

Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry SDK (auto-instrumented Flask backend) → OTEL Collector (OTLP gRPC :4317) → Tempo → Grafana with TraceQL queries (Trace ID, Span ID, duration, status, HTTP attributes)
Metrics with Prometheus: scraping prometheus_flask_exporter (:10000/metrics), kube-state-metrics (:8080), and cAdvisor built into K3s every 5s
Custom business metrics in Grafana: global RPS vs business RPS (filtering /health and /metrics), p95 and p50 latency, CPU and memory per pod, pod restarts
Public NodePort services: Frontend :30080, Backend :30100 (load balanced), Grafana :30000 — internal ClusterIP services for Redis, Prometheus, Tempo, and OTEL Collector
K8s resource management: requests and limits configured per service (backend: 256Mi–512Mi RAM, 100m–500m CPU) for saturation and OOMKilled testing
Resilience validation: resource saturation tests with real-time observation of scheduler and load balancer behavior

devops-azure.title: Containerization & CI/CD on Azure
devops-azure.subtitle: Automated Testing, Docker Packaging & Continuous Cloud Deployment
devops-azure.description: Full lifecycle automation for a web application (Next.js, Python Flask, and Redis): from pushing a code change to running automated tests and deploying on Microsoft Azure.
devops-azure.long_description:
Designed and implemented the containerization architecture and complete CI/CD workflow for SmartCatalog, a microservice-based web application consisting of a modern Next.js frontend (with React 19 and Tailwind CSS 4), a robust Python Flask API backend, and a high-speed caching and storage service with Redis. The project involved designing consistent environments using Docker and Docker Compose for local development, structuring a Continuous Integration (CI) pipeline in GitHub Actions to run automated backend tests with Pytest (utilizing a temporary in-memory Redis service).

We also configured a Continuous Deployment (CD) pipeline that automates the multi-stage Docker image build-and-push to Azure Container Registry (ACR) followed by dynamic deployment and orchestration on Azure Container Instances (ACI). This ensures that every push to the deployment branch securely automates the entire software life cycle on the Microsoft Azure cloud.
devops-azure.challenge: Deploying updates manually to a server often leads to human error, environment mismatches between developer laptops and production, and slow detection when a change breaks an existing feature.
devops-azure.solution: We packaged all three application services into identical Docker containers and built an automated GitHub Actions workflow: on every push, the system runs automated tests and deploys the updated containers to Microsoft Azure with zero manual steps.

highlights.label: Next.js Frontend, Flask API, and Redis in containers
Pytest suite and cloud deploy triggered on every push
Private Registry (ACR) + Elastic Containers (ACI)
Cloud storage configured so votes and stats never reset

key_features.title: Identical Environments Across Local & Cloud
key_features.description: With a single Docker Compose command, any developer spins up the web app, API, and database locally with the exact same configuration used in production.

key_features.title: Automated Quality Gate Before Release
key_features.description: Every time new code is pushed, GitHub Actions spins up a temporary test environment and runs automated tests to verify the API behaves properly.

key_features.title: Zero-Touch Deployment to Microsoft Azure
key_features.description: Once tests pass, the pipeline builds lightweight images, stores them in Azure's private registry, and updates the live cloud containers in minutes.

key_features.title: SmartCatalog App (Blind AI Model Voting)
key_features.description: Lets users blindly vote on which AI-generated product description reads best, displaying real-time model performance charts.

features: Multi-Service Containerization: Created optimized multi-stage Dockerfiles to build the Next.js (Node.js) frontend and Python Flask backend in isolation, minimizing final image sizes.

Local Orchestration with Docker Compose: Configured a reproducible local environment that links and securely connects the Frontend, Backend, and Redis service using secure passwords and persistence configured via environment variables.

Continuous Integration (CI) with Automated Testing: Developed a GitHub Actions pipeline that installs Python 3.11 dependencies, spins up a local Redis database on the runner, and executes API unit tests using Pytest.
Base Image Fallback Strategy: Automated the CD pipeline to pull, tag, and securely push official external images (such as Redis Alpine) to your private container registry.
Secure Registry with Azure Container Registry (ACR): Configured and authenticated secure Azure credentials in GitHub Actions to store built images safely and privately.
Automated Deployment to Azure Container Instances (ACI): Automated the dynamic creation and recreation of containers in the cloud using Azure CLI commands within GitHub Actions.
Cache Data Persistence: Configured persistent append-only storage (--appendonly yes) and password protection in the production Redis container deployed on the Azure cloud.

Environment Variable and Secret Management: Securely injected production secrets (database credentials, connection URLs, Redis passwords, and Supabase endpoints) at build and execution time without compromising security.

data-warehouse.clientOrContext: Information Systems Engineering — Enterprise Data Management (UTN-FRRe)
data-warehouse.title: Data Warehouse & BI: Record Label
data-warehouse.subtitle: Data Warehouse, ETL Pipelines, OLAP Cubes & Executive Power BI Dashboards
data-warehouse.description: End-to-end Business Intelligence solution transforming scattered music sales and production cost records into interactive executive dashboards for decision-making.
data-warehouse.long_description:
Developed a complete and robust Business Intelligence (BI) solution to optimize strategic decision-making for a record label distributing music records to global retail stores. The solution implements the three main stages of enterprise data analysis:

1) Dimensional Modeling (Part 1): Designed the conceptual and logical schemas utilizing the 'multidim' methodology and Microsoft SQL Server. Structured the Data Warehouse around two main fact tables (HechoVentas for retail orders and HechoProducciones for album launch costs) and eight normalized dimensions, ensuring daily granularity and referential integrity via surrogate default keys (-1).

2) ETL Integration (Part 2): Built automated extraction, transformation, and load (bulk and incremental idempotent) pipelines inside SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS), deploying a Staging Area for data scrubbing. Managed historical changes by applying Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD Type 1 for basic overwrites and Type 2 for active/ended validity ranges in DimArtista and DimBanda). Integrated location data cleansing using Data Quality Services (DQS).

3) Multidimensional Analysis & BI (Part 3): Engineered a multidimensional OLAP Cube in SQL Server Analysis Services (SSAS), configuring geographical and temporal hierarchies alongside custom calculated MDX measures (such as Unmet Demand and performance KPIs). Connected this analytical model to develop an interactive Power BI Executive Dashboard consolidating ROI metrics per artist/album, sales by music genre, and region-wide demand heatmaps using real-time Drill-down, Roll-up, Slice, and Dice operations.
data-warehouse.challenge: The record label held separate operational records for retail store orders, shipments, and studio production costs, making it difficult to see which albums or artists delivered the highest return on investment (ROI) or which regions had unfulfilled demand.
data-warehouse.solution: We built a complete SQL Server Data Warehouse with automated data cleansing and loading pipelines (ETL), a fast multidimensional OLAP cube, and an executive Power BI dashboard where leadership can filter sales, costs, and demand by country, year, genre, or band.

highlights.label: Dimensional Model, ETL Pipelines, and OLAP Cube
Retail store sales and album production costs
Historical tracking of artist and band changes
Interactive ROI, map, and demand dashboards

key_features.title: Automated Data Unification & Cleansing (ETL)
key_features.description: Consolidates data from multiple sources, standardizes country and location names automatically, and updates the warehouse without duplicating records.

key_features.title: Historical Change Tracking
key_features.description: Tracks when an artist or band changes attributes using effective date ranges so historical sales reports remain accurate.

key_features.title: Profitability & Unmet Demand Indicators
key_features.description: Automatically calculates Return on Investment (ROI) comparing production costs against sales, and highlights stores that ordered more records than shipped.

key_features.title: Interactive Executive Dashboard in Power BI
key_features.description: Clear visual reporting with geographical heatmaps, music genre rankings, and dynamic filters to drill down from yearly totals to daily details.

features: Business Dimensional Modeling: Conceptual and physical design using the 'multidim' methodology, structuring a Data Warehouse with two fact tables and eight interconnected dimensions.
Granularity Management: Defined daily granularity for HechoVentas (retail store orders, agreed prices, shipped quantities) and HechoProducciones (album production costs and launch dates).

Bulk Loading & SSIS Idempotency: Developed Integration Services (SSIS) packages prepared for automatic reprocessing via pre-load truncating and controlled surrogate default key insertion (-1 for nulls).

Layered Dimension Loading: Orchestrated sequential load flows in SSIS, processing leaf dimensions (Location, Instrument, Category, Manager) first, followed by dependent dimensions (Store, Band, Artist, Record).
Business Logic & Mock Data: Implemented SSIS data flow algorithms to automatically assign band representatives (lead artist if no manager is present) and generate missing dates in DimTiempo.
High-Efficiency Incremental Load: Designed periodic incremental load pipelines for HechoVentas and HechoProducciones by identifying data deltas via LastUpdatedDate to prevent duplication.

Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD): Maintained strict historical tracking by applying SCD Type 1 (overwriting personal attributes) and Type 2 (generating new versions with effective 'from/to' dates in DimArtista and DimBanda).
Data Cleansing with DQS: Integrated SQL Server Data Quality Services (DQS) steps to clean, standardize, and enrich country names and subdivisions in the Location dimension.
Multidimensional SSAS OLAP Cubes: Designed and deployed multidimensional databases in Analysis Services (SSAS) with optimized data source views and complex attribute hierarchies.
MDX Calculated Measures: Programmed custom business metrics inside the cube, such as 'Unmet Demand' (Ordered vs Shipped) and performance KPIs to measure sales targets.
Interactive Power BI Dashboard: Constructed a dynamic executive dashboard featuring geolocalized heatmaps, album sales rankings, top genres by revenue, and unified KPI cards.

Interactive OLAP Operations: Demonstrated and implemented analytical workflows inside Power BI using Drill-down navigation, Roll-up aggregations, Slice filtering, and multi-dimensional Dice combinations.

play-finder.clientOrContext: ADUSI Capstone Project — UTN Resistencia Regional Faculty
play-finder.title: Play Finder
play-finder.subtitle: Sports Court Booking Platform, Complex Management & Analytics
play-finder.description: Web platform connecting players with sports complexes: search live court availability, book time slots online, and manage schedules and revenue.
play-finder.long_description:
Play Finder is a responsive Full Stack web platform designed to optimize and simplify the booking of sports courts, seamlessly connecting complex owners with sports players. Developed collaboratively by a team of 7 people over 8 three-week sprints using Scrum methodology, it served as the Capstone Project for the University Software Developer Analyst (ADUSI) program at UTN-FRRe.

The system supports two primary user flows: an owner portal (to manage sports complexes, customize courts, manage hourly pricing, and view dashboard analytics such as popular booking hours and occupancy periods) and a player portal (featuring advanced search, live scheduling, booking confirmation, credit card payment simulation, and automated email notifications). The platform was containerized and deployed on Microsoft Azure.
play-finder.challenge: Booking a sports court often requires back-and-forth calls or messages to check open times, while complex owners spend hours manually writing down reservations and dealing with double-bookings.
play-finder.solution: We built a two-sided web platform: a player portal to search courts by sport, date, and time and book immediately with email confirmation; and an owner portal to configure courts, pricing, and view occupancy statistics.

highlights.label: Player Booking Experience & Owner Dashboard
Automatic validation preventing double-bookings
Peak hour reports and bookings by time period
Collaborative Scrum development deployed on Azure

key_features.title: Live Court Search & Availability
key_features.description: Players filter sports complexes by discipline (soccer, padel, basketball), date, and time slot, seeing only genuinely available courts.

key_features.title: Online Booking & Automated Email Receipts
key_features.description: Guided reservation flow with simulated deposit checkout, Google sign-in, and instant confirmation sent via email.

key_features.title: Complex, Court & Pricing Administration
key_features.description: Owners register their venues, upload photos, define surface types for each court, and configure opening hours and hourly rates.

key_features.title: Owner Analytics Dashboard
key_features.description: Displays clear charts of the most popular booking hours and reservation volume over time to support business decisions.

features: Decoupled Full Stack architecture: Interactive React.js frontend styled with Chakra UI and a robust Node.js backend using Express and TypeScript.
Relational database modeling with PostgreSQL and Prisma ORM, ensuring high referential integrity and optimized queries for nested complex-to-court relations.
Sports Complex Management: Full CRUD operations for sports complexes, including business hours, location details, and multimedia assets.
Court Administration: Custom configuration for turf/surface type, sports disciplines (soccer, tennis, basketball), custom pricing, and dynamic calendar availability.
Advanced Search & Filtering: Real-time query module enabling players to discover sports complexes and filter available courts by date, time, and sport.
Interactive Booking System: Robust scheduling pipeline featuring strict backend validations to prevent double-booking or slot overlaps.
Mock Payment Gateway: Simulated checkout flow for booking deposits or full payments with interactive credit card validation.
Robust Security & Auth: Secure user accounts using JSON Web Tokens (JWT) and third-party social login with Google OAuth, backed by custom router middleware.
Email Notifications: Seamless SendGrid API integration to automate booking confirmation emails and secure password recovery flows.
Analytical Dashboard: Rich analytics suite for complex owners showcasing bar charts of peak hours, popular days, and cumulative booking revenue.
DevOps Containerization: Microservices deployed as Docker containers hosted on Azure Container Apps with a PostgreSQL cloud database on Azure.
Scrum Agile Workflow: Full project lifecycle managed, tracked, and refined across 8 successive sprints using Jira Software.
play-finder.arch_desc: Play Finder is engineered using a decoupled, modular, and highly robust architecture, organizing the Node.js, Express, and TypeScript backend under the Repository-Service-Handler design pattern. HTTP requests flow from the client to the Express Handler, which delegates business logic to the Services layer, and finally persists data using Prisma ORM inside the Repository layer. The frontend is a Single Page Application (SPA) built with React, Chakra UI, and Vite, which efficiently fetches and synchronizes state in real time using custom hooks driven by TanStack Query.
play-finder.db_desc: The PostgreSQL relational database schema was meticulously designed and normalized to guarantee referential integrity. The final model (Sprint 8) maps precise cardinalities among users, subscription plans, complexes, courts, day-to-day schedules, and booking records with payment transactions, enabling high-performance queries and procedural analytics dashboards.
